property_summary: For any inputs to initialize(...), the correct contract sets c.nft() equal to the _nft argument passed to initialize; the mutant instead sets nft to the factory-derived owner address for some inputs, so there exist inputs where c.nft() != _nft.

For every call to initialize(...) the contract's public nft() equals the _nft argument passed in (reference satisfies this for all inputs); the mutant sets nft to a different address (the factory owner) for some inputs, so there exist inputs where c.nft() != _nft.

For every call to initialize(...), the reference contract stores the exact _nft argument in c.nft(); the mutant sometimes stores a different address (the factory.ownerOf(...) result) so there exist inputs where c.nft() != the _nft argument.

For every call to initialize(...), the reference contract sets c.nft() to the _nft argument passed; the mutant instead may set c.nft() to an address derived from the factory (Factory(factory).ownerOf(...)) for some inputs, so there exist init arguments where c.nft() != the provided _nft.

For every call to initialize(...), the reference contract stores in c.nft() an address whose ownerOf on the factory (when interpreted as an ERC721 token id equal to the pool address cast to uint160) is irrelevant — concretely the reference always sets c.nft() equal to the _nft argument passed to initialize, while the mutant sets c.nft() to Factory(factory).ownerOf(uint160(address(this))) for some inputs, so there exist fuzzed _nft values where after initialize the stored nft != the provided _nft.

For every valid initialize(...) call the reference contract sets feeRate equal to the _feeRate argument (i.e. feeRate() == _feeRate after initialize), whereas the mutant defers setting feeRate until after initialized which can cause feeRate to remain zero during initialization-observable calls and thus break this property for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, after initialize returns the public getter feeRate() equals the provided _feeRate; the mutant that delays setting feeRate can cause intermediate calls during initialize (triggered via a reentrant receiver on safeTransferFrom when transferring an ERC721 into the contract during initialization) to observe feeRate() == 0, breaking the rule for some inputs.

For every call to initialize(...) the contract's public feeRate() getter equals the _feeRate argument after initialization completes; the mutant that moves setting feeRate until after initialized allows a reentrant ERC721 receiver called during initialization to observe feeRate() == 0 (breaking the rule for some inputs).
